newsitem.title: USA: Chicago mayor proposes $200 mln neighborhood bonds.
newsitem.headline: Chicago mayor proposes $200 mln neighborhood bonds.

text.p: Chicago Mayor Richard Daley on Monday proposed issuing $200 million in debt to fund a wideranging neighborhood repair program.
The proceeds of the issue would go to accelerating the pace of improvements to basic residential streets, sidewalks, alleys and curbs, Daley stated in a news release.
Daley also proposed to cut property taxes $20 million and eliminate a business head tax in Chicago by the year 2000 by first cutting it from $4 per employee to $2 per employee next year.

The proposed changes would be funded by reforming the city's employee pension policies, Daley said. The changes are expected to save the city $56 million per year, allowing for the neighborhood repairs and property tax cuts, the release added.
Under the repair program, Chicago will double new alley and street construction, increase landscaping projects and begin replacing entire blocks of vaulted sidewalks, Daley stated.

The proposed changes to the police and fire pensions require legislative approval of alterations to the city's required employer contributions. The city also proposes early retirement incentives for city employees in the first half of 1998.
